title: Single-bit priority for longest impossible differentials in larger SIMON
summary: Prove or refute that single-bit endpoint differences always contain a longest direct-contradiction impossible differential for each larger SIMON block-size variant.

formal_statement.body: For each $v\in\{48,64,96,128\}$, let $L_v$ be the maximum round length of a SIMON-$v$ impossible differential under the source's fixed-key direct-contradiction and practical-boundary model, and let $L_v^{(1)}$ be the same maximum restricted to single-bit input and output differences. Is $L_v^{(1)}=L_v$ for all four values of $v$? Prove all four equalities or give a counterexample requiring a non-single-bit endpoint.

scope.domain: Impossible differential cryptanalysis of SIMON48, SIMON64, SIMON96, and SIMON128
assumptions: The fixed-key direct-contradiction model is the one defined by the source
The longest-round comparison uses the source practical-boundary convention
The restricted representatives have single-bit input and output differences
scope.unresolved_remainder: Later tools find large clusters and recover known round lengths only inside restricted models or search spaces. None proves representative completeness or supplies a longer multi-bit counterexample for any of SIMON48, SIMON64, SIMON96, or SIMON128.

progress.summary: The source leaves the transfer of SIMON32 single-bit priority to all four larger SIMON block sizes open.
